items.stem: Who is the first figure of myth the Chorus compares to Antigone?
How did Zeus come to Danaë?
options: As a white bull from the sea

items.stem: Complete the Chorus's line: “Daughter of _____ in her sire’s vast caves”
Who brought Dryas' child to a rocky dungeon?
Where was the Edonian king imprisoned?
options: In a tower of brass by the sea

items.stem: How many step-sons suffered, according to line 913?
Swift as whose horses did the step-mother speed over the hills?
Whom does the Chorus address as my child?
What does Danaë's cell become, in line 887?
options: A royal throne room of gold

items.stem: Complete the Chorus's line: “On Bosporus’ lone _____”
What does the phrase “To cool the madness of a fevered brain” suggest?
options: The prison was meant to calm his frenzy
He was sick with a fever caught at sea long ago

items.stem: What did the Edonian king try to quench?
options: A burning city on the plain

items.stem: From whose race did the step-mother descend?
What does “the tuneful Nine” refer to?
What do Danaë and Antigone have in common, according to the ode?
options: Love for a prince of Thebes
A gift for song and dance at feasts

items.stem: What does “the Maenad’s fire” refer to in line 904?
options: A fire set by Theban soldiers
The flame burning on the altar of Zeus

items.stem: What does the image of “brass-prowed ships, that breast the sea” add to the ode?
options: Human strength and skill offer no refuge
Sea travel is the safest way to escape
Ships were built near Danaë's tower of brass

items.stem: Complete the Chorus's line: “Wasting away they mourned their piteous _____”
Which word best describes the ode's attitude toward the sufferers of myth?
How does the story of the Edonian king differ from Danaë's?
options: He was punished for his own insolence
He was shut away by his father for being beautiful

items.stem: What does the phrase “exchanged the glad sunlight For a cell” stress?
options: Her loss of light and freedom
Her joy at finding a new home

items.stem: What is the effect of addressing Antigone as “my child” twice?
options: It adds tenderness to the warning
It shows that the elders are her parents by blood
It shows open anger at her

items.stem: How is the ode structured?
options: As three stories, each ending in suffering
As one long prayer to Zeus
As a debate between two singers
As a list of Theban kings and their many deeds

items.stem: What does the step-mother's “spindle red” with gore suggest?
options: A household tool turned into a weapon
A sign of her skill at weaving
A symbol of her royal blood and noble race

items.stem: What tension does the ode create by pairing innocent Danaë with the insolent Edonian king?
options: It leaves unclear whether Antigone suffers innocently or for pride
It proves beyond doubt that Antigone is innocent
It praises the king for his courage
It shows that Fate rewards the virtuous in the end and punishes the proud

items.stem: Complete the Chorus's line: “And of the tuneful Nine provoked the _____.”
How does naming Ares as witness to the blinding add to the ode's mood?
options: It links the cruelty to war and bloodshed
It shows that the gods stepped in to prevent it
It shows the sons were warriors

items.stem: What is the effect of the ode's dense allusions for its first audience?
options: They call up familiar stories of suffering
They hide the meaning from the elders
They introduce many new characters to the plot

items.stem: The ode's tone toward Fate is best described as
What does “A child of gods; yet she” was vanquished imply about Antigone?
options: Noble birth will not save her
She will be rescued by the gods
